 Apple iOS 27.2 arrives soon: 7 new features on the way
 Your iPhone is getting some new features with the latest iOS. 
  By 
 Matt Binder 
 Matt Binder 
 Senior Tech Reporter 
 Matt Binder joined Mashable's tech vertical in 2018, where he covers social media, tech policy, cybersecurity, online scams, cryptocurrency, AI, creator news, weird tech, and other related tech beats.
 Read Full Bio 
  on  October 22, 2026 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Flipboard 
 Here's a look at the 6 best new features coming to iPhone with the release of iOS 27.2. 
 Credit: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images 
 With the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max now available and the iPhone Duo launch just around the corner (our full iPhone Duo review is online ), Apple is also prepping its latest iOS update for its mobile devices.
 Along with various bug fixes, the new iOS 27.2 is also going to be packed with new features as well. The update is expected to launch before the end of October; it could come any minute now.
 Here are the biggest new features headed your way in iOS 27.2.
 You May Also Like 
 Dual Capture for group FaceTime calls
 Dual Capture allows users with compatible iPhone models to capture a video simultaneously with both their rear main camera and selfie camera. Dual Capture for FaceTime allows users to utilize both the front and rear camera when on a FaceTime video call, but this feature only works with a call with an individual person.
 Now, 9to5Mac reports that with iOS 27.2, users will be able to utilize Dual Capture when on Group FaceTime calls, too.
 Redesigned Health app
 Apple showed off the new Health app at its September event when it unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and iPhone Duo. It will finally arrive with the rollout of iOS 27.2, per MacRumors .
 The redesigned Health app is now organized into three main tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. Insights includes vitals, heart rate, and other related current health information, whereas the Longevity tab includes your health data over a period of time.
 Suggestions in Messages
 Messages is getting a new feature that offers suggestions based on the context of a conversation in your texts. For example, if a contact texts you about a date for an event, Suggestions will provide one-tap options to add that event to your calendar or set up a reminder.  9to5 Mac reports this feature will finally arrive on iPhones that support Apple Intelligence with iOS 27.2

 With this feature, Messages can also help users find photos, locations, contacts, and other pertinent information as it relates to the context of the conversation.
 Interestingly, Suggestions was included in the original iOS 27 beta, but was later pulled, according to 9to5Mac . This is also a case of Apple playing catch-up, as Galaxy and Pixel phones already have this AI feature (it's called Magic Cue on Pixel phones and Now Nudge on Galaxy phones ).

 The best smartphones of 2026: Compare Apple, Galaxy, and Pixel's best 
 Revamped 'Up Next' in Apple Podcasts
 Apple is splitting up the "Up Next" section in Apple Podcasts into two different sections, according to MacRumors .
 New Episodes will appear where Up Next is currently, and show users the latest episodes for the podcasts that they subscribe to. Continue Playing is a brand new section that will appear below New Episodes and will display all episodes in the queue that the user was listening to. 
 Anniversaries via Call Context
 This isn't a huge new feature, but it could be a fun one. If you have an anniversary set up with someone in your Contacts, the new Call Context feature will remind you of this fact if that contact calls you at that time. You can see this feature in action at MacRumors .
 Profiles on Apple TV app
 It's incredible that it took this long for this to happen, but the Apple TV app on iOS will now support user profiles. (We're also expecting Apple to release a new Apple TV device in early October.)
 Apple TV viewers on tvOS have long been able to create separate user profiles, which include different movie and TV show suggestions based on the user's watch history. This same ability did not exist on iPhone until now, with the upcoming release of iOS 27.2, also per MacRumors .
 New Home app alerts
 This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.
 Apple is all set to launch some new smart home products this fall, including the brand new HomeView smart speaker. The Apple Home app will be critical to managing these new devices, and so it's no surprise that some updates are coming. In addition to new products, Apple is also giving the Home app in iOS 27.2 a couple of new functions to help keep your home safe and in order.
 First is "Lock After Closing," a new feature that, well, automatically locks a door after it's been closed but not locked. You can set a specific duration of time that needs to pass before the door automatically locks, and it's supported by products like the LG Smart Deadbolt Lock . 
 Similarly, "Door Left Open" is an alert that automatically notifies users when a door equipped with a compatible smart lock has been left open for too long. If you want to make sure every door in your house is closed when they should be closed, iOS 27.2 has your back.
